meta.title: Spotlight Search
meta.description: Async content search with category tabs, recent history, and rich result cards. Triggered by / — distinct from Command Palette, which handles actions. Results come from your API.

blocks.content: Command Palette is for actions — navigate to a page, run a command, trigger a shortcut. Spotlight Search is for content — find a user by name, locate a document, search across project records. The results come from your database, update on every keystroke, and group by content type.

SpotlightRoot debounces the query (280ms), fires onSearch with an AbortSignal, and cancels in-flight requests when the query changes. Results group under category headers when multiple categories return matches. Recent searches persist to localStorage and show when the input is empty.

blocks.title: vs Command Palette
blocks.content: Install both and they coexist: Command Palette on ⌘K for actions, Spotlight on / for search. They are separate systems with separate state — opening one doesn't affect the other.
Press / or click the button to open. Try searching for alice, dashboard, form, or guide. Results group by People, Projects, and Docs. Recent searches persist between opens.
Wrap your app in SpotlightRoot. Pass your categories and an onSearch function. The function receives the query and an AbortSignal — pass the signal to fetch so requests cancel when the query changes.

Each result has a category field matching a SpotlightCategory id. When results span multiple categories, they appear under separate headers. Category tabs allow filtering to one type. The All tab is always present.

Results with a category id that doesn't match any SpotlightCategory still appear under the All tab — they just won't have a dedicated category tab or header label. This is intentional: you can return mixed results without pre-declaring every category.

When the input is empty, Spotlight shows recent search queries. Each one can be dismissed individually or cleared entirely. Clicking a recent query fills the input and fires the search. Persists to localStorage under storageKey.
